claims.statement: The member frontend is the browser-facing Next.js App Router application for coach conversations; it owns session-aware UI, member thread operations, chat projection, and presentation, but it is not the authorization authority — the downstream member perimeter authorizes the Supabase identity and thread ownership, while browser checks and the proxy's bearer-format/thread probes only improve the boundary.

`/chat` first obtains the Supabase session in the browser; a missing email or session lookup failure redirects to `/login`, the cached CopilotKit Authorization header is refreshed before rendering, and only then is the CopilotKit v2 provider mounted in multi-route mode (`useSingleEndpoint={false}`) targeting agent `coach` at the same-origin `/api/copilotkit` endpoint, with production dependencies constructed only after this gate.

The catch-all `/api/copilotkit` route builds a CopilotKit runtime with a `LangGraphAgent` for graph `coach` and an `InMemoryAgentRunner`; its `onRequest` hook is the sole every-route gate rejecting any request whose `Authorization` header is missing or malformed with 401 before routing, and default header forwarding (not a platform key) carries the bearer to the LangGraph deployment.

`CoachLangGraphAgent` overrides `getSchemaKeys()` to return a pinned member-visible schema (`question`, `attachment_id`, `ag-ui`, `copilotkit` inputs and `messages` output) because the OSS agent server keeps `/assistants/:id/schemas` at 501, preventing AG-UI's HTTP-error fallback from dropping the question and adapter markers.

The runtime's in-memory thread list is global rather than member-scoped, so `GET /api/copilotkit/threads` is intentionally answered as an empty page while the sidebar reads threads through the direct member thread API instead.

For any URL-addressed thread, stop operation, or run/connect request naming a body `threadId`, the proxy first performs `GET /threads/{id}` upstream with the same bearer via `authorizeThreadAccess`; an inaccessible or erased thread is answered with a uniform 404 (same shape as a perimeter denial) before the runtime can read, stop, connect, or recreate it, because every legitimate thread is created through the direct member surface before its first run.

The `/api/copilotkit` proxy logs only method, pathname, status, and an unverified JWT `sub` used solely for correlation; it never logs request bodies, query values, or bearer tokens, and the decoded `sub` is never used as an authorization decision.

`useCoachStream.ts` is the chat controller and takes an injected `CoachChatDeps` bundle (network, timing, polling, and ID seams) so component tests can drive the full lifecycle from scripted fakes with zero real network or timers; production wiring is constructed once in `coachClient.ts`.

The browser protocol client is split across `coachApi.ts` (the direct HTTP/SDK client shaping every member-facing call byte-for-byte to the member perimeter contract mirrored in `coachProtocol.ts`) and `stream.ts` (the pure `applyStreamPart()` reducer that folds one AG-UI/LangGraph SDK stream event into `{messages, interruptValue}`), with `coachClient.ts` wiring both plus the CopilotKit headless engine into `useCoachStream`.

The stream reducer only reads updates for nodes in `coachProtocol.ts`'s `RENDERED_NODE_NAMES` allow-list (`coach_gate`, `coach_agent`, `erase_my_data`, `reminder_delivery`, `claim_document`, `review_document`, `finalize_coach`); updates from any other node are dropped and reported via `chatTelemetry({kind: "unknown_node"})`, and human messages arriving through the stream are ignored because the human bubble is a local echo.

The stream reducer treats the AG-UI `__interrupt__` event and an in-band `{"__interrupt__": [...]}` payload inside an `updates` event identically, both producing an `interruptValue` via `firstInterruptValue`, because the Agent Server delivers interrupts inside the updates stream rather than as a distinct event.

Thread state reads are merged with live stream messages by stable message identity via `model.ts`'s `mergeMessages()`, then split into HumanMessage-bounded turns via `buildTurns()`, which also extracts per-turn DATA envelopes for catalog hydration.

Switching threads clears the agent messages and controller state before the newly selected thread is reloaded, preventing the prior conversation from bleeding into the next one; selection triggers exactly one thread reconnection rather than stacking connections, and the controller supports non-cancelling detach/disconnect with subsequent rejoin.

A send creates a thread when necessary, echoes the human message locally, and starts a run; while a run is active, later sends are appended to a FIFO queue (`enqueueSend`/`queue` state) and drained one at a time once the controller is idle, avoiding overlapping runs on one thread.

`regenerateEligibility()` restricts regeneration/branch/feedback to the latest HumanMessage-bounded turn only: it is disabled when that turn has tool activity, a ToolMessage, a pending interrupt, an erase marker, an unanswered question, or the document-review sentinel question — never an older turn.

`NEXT_PUBLIC_HC_RAG_MEMBER_STREAM_PERIMETER` is a build-time public compatibility flag whose value must match the deployed member perimeter's stream protocol: the default/v1 mode streams updates only over non-resumable streams and rejects multitasking, while `v2` streams updates plus messages over resumable streams with `multitaskStrategy: "enqueue"`, enabling rejoin and checkpoint-based fork/edit/regenerate paths.

History, time-travel, and visible branching controls require the separate opt-in `NEXT_PUBLIC_COACH_HISTORY_BRANCH_UI=1`; the underlying controller operations remain callable when this UI gate is off.

`CoachToolRenderers` is mounted once inside the CopilotKit provider (in `app/chat/page.tsx`) and registers the tool, interrupt, medical, envelope, clipboard, and fallback renderers via `useRenderTool`/`useInterrupt`/`useFrontendTool`.

Catalog rendering is fail-closed end to end: `compose_ui` trees must pass the wire schema, render only after a correlated successful ToolMessage (a correlated error suppresses the tree in favor of textual output), hydrate `__ref` fact props only from a same-turn-scope DATA envelope with RFC 6901 pointer resolution (cross-turn matches are explicitly rejected as `cross_turn`), dispatch button/action ids only through the fixed `DISPATCH_ACTIONS` map (unknown or unregistered ids are telemetry no-ops), and any failing node renders nothing while sibling nodes still render.

The composable catalog registry is exactly 11 components (`InjectionTracker`, `MiniCalendar`, `TrendCard`, `ActionCard`, `StatRow`, `ScoreRing`, `Timeline`, `Card`, `Tag`, `Label`, `Button`); the four fixed-contract cards (`CalendarChangeCard`, `MemoryExtractionCard`, `DocumentIngestCard`, `ReminderCard`) are explicitly not part of this catalog and instead render directly from interrupts, upload status, or envelopes.

Every fact-bearing catalog prop must be a `{__ref: {turn_scope_id, block_id, pointer}}` data reference (`DataRefSchema`) — the wire zod schema rejects literal fact props — while static labels/actions remain literals under a fixed allow-list; only schema-recognized calendar-change and memory-extraction interrupts display approval cards, whose `{accept, fields?}` responses are validated before resolve.

The direct `coachApi.ts` surface is limited to member thread CRUD (`createThread`, `searchThreads`, `getThread`, `deleteThread`, `copyThread`), state/history (`getThreadState`), upload/status (`postUpload`, `getUploadStatus`), feedback (`postFeedback`), and run-related endpoints (`streamRun`); a thrown `CoachApiError` always carries the HTTP status, and cron/assistant-search/store endpoints are never called from this app.

`createCoachFetch()` and the LangGraph SDK request hook retrieve the Supabase access token per request rather than relying on a page-load cached token; `supabaseAccessToken()`-style refresh triggers when under one minute of validity remains, so direct member API calls always carry a fresh bearer.

Attachments progress only through server-reported stages (`uploading`, `scanning`, `extracting`, `done`) using the fixed document-review sentinel question; client polling advances state solely from returned status, never from local timers.

Client-driven erasure phase 2 (`runErasePhase2`) begins only after the server-side marker flow reaches terminality; it fully snapshots paginated owned threads in ascending thread-id order, deletes non-marker threads first, deletes the marker-bearing current thread last, and is fail-stop by design: any DELETE failure preserves remaining IDs (including the marker thread) so a retry can resume from the persisted marker.

The frontend runs on Bun with scripts `dev`, `build`, `start`, `test`, and `playwright`; the test command `bun --cwd frontend run test` executes `vitest run` in a jsdom environment with `@/*` aliased to `src/*` and tests collected under `src/**/*.test.{ts,tsx}` per `vitest.config.ts`, and this JavaScript/TypeScript toolchain is entirely separate from the Python backend's pytest-based suite (no shared dependency manifest, configuration, or invocation path).

Browser-visible configuration is restricted to `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` values (Supabase URL, Supabase anonymous key, public LangGraph URL, and explicit UI/protocol gates); secrets, service-role credentials, LangSmith keys, and deployment tokens must never be placed in `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` variables because Next embeds them in the browser bundle, while the server-only proxy obtains its deployment target from `LANGGRAPH_DEPLOYMENT_URL` (accepting the public URL as an alias) and fails only when first used if unconfigured.

The hermetic Playwright suite boots an offline scripted gateway, a real `langgraph dev` server, and a production `next start`, all on allocated ports, with zero external network calls; it intentionally runs with a single worker because fixture state and the single ephemeral stack are order-dependent.
